What really hooked me is not a specific system but the psychological shift created by the overall pacing. At first I always tried to push forward quickly and paid the price for bad judgment. Over time I learned to pause before acting and observe the environment more carefully. The game does not punish slowness and often rewards patience. Eventually I stopped caring about how much I gained and focused on finishing cleanly. That calm feeling after a successful run feels more convincing than any flashy success message. It is not emotionally loud but it stays with you long after you stop playing

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (78%): players like the gameplay and combat.
Cheating is the top complaint, and some players will not recommend the game until it is fixed.

details.text: Complaints about cheaters have eased recently, falling to 12% of recent reviews from 19% of all reviews, though cheating is still the main worry.
Players with under 2 hours are far less positive than those with over fifty hours, so newcomers are the least likely group to recommend it.
